title: Why Is Sports Betting So Male? An Economist Points to a 2001 Study Called “Boys Will Be Boys”
summary:
On the Optimist Economy podcast, economist Kathryn Anne Edwards pointed to a landmark finance study to explain why betting apps, crypto, and speculative markets skew so heavily male.
The study is “Boys Will Be Boys,” which Brad Barber and Terrance Odean published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics in 2001.

title: Asian stock markets climb after earlier tech rout
summary:
Markets rebound after tech rout triggered by Democrats’ sweeping victory in US midterm elections.
Asian stock markets have rebounded after last week’s tech rout triggered by the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.
Key indexes in Japan, Taiwan and Australia rose on Monday, following a rebound on Wall Street on Friday.
In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 2.33 percent, while the S&P/ASX 200 in Sydney edged up 0.099 percent.
The tech rout spilled into Asia on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 and KOSPI plunging about 6 percent and 9 percent, respectively, and the Hang Seng Index dropping more than 1 percent.

title: US Adds 165,000 Jobs in October: Why Bitcoin Traders Are Watching the Fed
summary:
The data complicate hopes of quick monetary easing, but the report by itself cannot establish what the Federal Reserve will do next or where Bitcoin will trade.
Rather, employment data are one part of the evidence the Federal Reserve weighs when deciding whether inflation and economic activity justify changing interest rates.
The important next readings include inflation releases, future employment revisions and Federal Reserve communications.
For now, October’s jobs report provides a firmer data point in the interest-rate debate.
